full_judgment:
Fatema Najib J: These First Appeal No. 212 of 2009, First Appeal No. 230 of 2009, Transfer Appeal No. 1 of 2014 and Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014 are directed against the judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008 passed by learned Joint District Judge, Third Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 51 of 2001, Title Suit No. 93 of 2014 and Title Suit No. 52 of 2001 which were heard analogously and now are being disposed of by this single judgment.

2. The respondent Nos. 1-3 of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 32 of 1997, in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Golapgonj, Sylhet impleading principal respondents Nos.4 and 5 as principal defendant Nos. 1 and 2, pro-forma respondent Nos. 6 and 7 as pro-forma defendant Nos. 3 and 4, Abdus Sattar, the predecessor of appellants Nos. 1 and 2 as the defendant Nos. 5 and appellants Nos.3-13 as 6-16 Nos. defendants for redemption of mortgage and khas possession in respect of 0.34 acres of land as described in schedule to plaint. Subsequently, it was transferred to the Joint District Judge Third Court, Sylhet and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 51 of 2001. The respondent No. 3 Pulin Ram Malakar died during the pendency of appeal and his legal heirs have been duly substituted. The plaintiff No.1 Gakul Ram Malakar of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997 (re-number as 51 of 2001) died during the pendency of the suit and his legal heir Nikhil Ram Malakar has been duly substituted as plaintiff No. 1(ka).

3. The appellant Nos. 1 and 2 of Title Appeal No. 147 of 2009 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 14 of 1994 in the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Sylhet impleading Abdus Sattar, the predecessor of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as defendant Nos. 2, respondents Nos.3-12 as defendants Nos. 3-12, Seraj the predecessor of respondent Nos. 13-17 as defendant No. 13, the respondent Nos. 18 to 24 as defendant Nos. 14-20 praying for partition in respect of 0.7 acres of land as described in schedule 1, declaration of right, title and interest in respect of second schedule property to the plaint. It may be mentioned that the heirs of Abdur Rahman who are also appellants in this Title Appeal No.147 of 2009 were added as plaintiffs 3-7 in the original suit by order No.144 dated 18-11-2008. During pendency of the suit the defendant Nos. 13 and 16 died whose legal heirs has been duly substituted. Subsequently, it was transferred to Joint District Judge, First court, Sylhet and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 93 of 2014. The said Title Appeal No.147 of 2009 was ultimately transferred to the High Court Division by Order dated 14-5-2012 passed in Civil Miscellaneous Case No.16 of 2010 and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No.1 of 2014.

4. The heirs of Seraj (defendant No.13) of the said Title Suit No. 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 as appellants filed First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 against the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 as pro-forma respondent Nos. 4, 5 and the defendants Nos. 19-20 as pro-forma respondent Nos. 6 and 7, the defendant Nos. 3-12, and 15 as respondent Nos. 8-16, Gakul Ram Malakar, the predecessor of the defendant No.16, the defendant Nos.17 and 18 as principal respondents 1-3.

5. The appellant No. 2, the predecessor of appellant No. 1, the predecessor of appellant Nos. 3-6 of Title Appeal No.108 of 2009 as plaintiff Nos. 1-3 instituted Title Suit No.15 of 1994 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Golapgonj, Sylhet impleading the respondents as defendants Nos. 1-22 for declaration of title by adverse possession for more than 12 years of the statutory period, correction of record in respect of first schedule to plaint as shail in place of canel and Khas possession in respect of second Schedule to plaint. Subsequently, it was transferred to the Sub-Judge, Third Court, Sylhet and re-numbered as Title Suit No.52 of 2001. The said Title Appeal No.108 of 2009 was transferred to the High Court Division by Order dated 14-5-2012 passed in Civil Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 2010 and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014.

6. The case of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997/51 of 2001 who are the defendant Nos.16-18 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 is that Gagan Ram Malakar, Raman Ram Malakar, and Avoy Ram Malakar who are successive owners by in-heritance of the suit land and subsequently executed and registered a sale deed on 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS in favour of Jahir Ali, (the predecessor of the defendant Nos.1 and 2) receiving Taka 100 as consideration money in respect of suit land and on the same date Jahir Ali executed a registered Ekrarnama in favour of the aforesaid Gagan Ram Malakar and others in respect of the same suit land promising to reconvey the suit land to the vendors on repayment of the consideration money within, 30th chaitra, 1361 BS. The transaction was not a sale, it was a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of 7 years in accordance with the provisions of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and after the expiry of 7 years it was redeemable by operation of law. The plaintiffs on several times requested the defendants to redeem the mortgage by receiving the consideration money. But the defendants refused to comply on the end of Bhadra, 1400 BS. Hence the plaintiff is constrained to file the present suit.

7. The heirs of Jahir Ali that is Md Manik Mia and Mst. Sabiya Begum the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 who are the defendant Nos.1 and 2 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 in brief their case is that Raman Ram Malakar, Gagan Ram Malakar and Ador Ram Malakar were owners of the first schedule land and while possessing the first schedule land Raman Ram Malakar and his two aforesaid brothers sold the first schedule land to Jahir Ali, (the predecessor of the plaintiffs) on 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11 Baisakh 1359 BS through a saf kabala. After getting the scheduled land they paid rent regularly to Zamidar. While possessing the first schedule land, Jahir Ali Sold 0.33 acres of land out of the land as described in first schedule land to Abdur Rahman (the predecessor of 4-12 defendants), the defendant Nos.1-3 on different dates by saf kabala and Jahir Ali has been possessing the remaining 0.07 acres of land by constructing tin shed building where made a tea-stall for long years. Subsequently, he died leaving behind the plaintiff No.1 as son and the plaintiff No. 2 as daughter. Later on the aforesaid Md Manik Mia and Mst Sabiya Begum came to know that on 24-4-1952 Gagan Ram Malakar and his two brothers executed a sale deed, in respect of suit land in favour of Jahir Ali who also executed ekrarnama (deed of agreement) promising to recovery the land to the vendors on repayment of the consideration money within 30th Chaitra 1361 BS corresponding to 24-4-1946. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by running tea-stall. The defendant Nos. 4-12 recently started construction a new building in first schedule of the plaint and threatened the defendants to destroy their restaurant from the suit land. In the meantime the defendants through Daroga of local thana on 8-5-1994 issued a notice alleging that the plaintiffs are illegal possessor and the plaintiffs are restraining the defendant No.4 from constructing. After getting the said notice the plaintiffs requested the defendant No. 4 on 9-5-1994 for partition in respect of 0.07 acres. But the defendant No. 4 refused the request. The plaintiffs have been possessing the second schedule land which is included of first schedule for more than 12 years of the statutory period since their predecessors. But the land of second schedule was inadvertently recorded in the name of the defendant No.14 in separate khatian and Mouja. The plaintiffs came to know on first part of January, 1994 that 0.34 acres of first schedule was recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs on RS Dag No. 2771 of RS Khatian No. 557. Since the defendant No.14 in collusion of defendant No. 4 refused the title of the plaintiffs, it clouded the right, title and interest of the plaintiff. Hence, the plaintiffs constrained to file the instant suit.

8. The defendant Nos. 1 and 5-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 contested the suit by filing separate written statement. The contents of defendant Nos.1 and 5-16 are almost same. It is contended by the defendant Nos. 5-16 that they purchased the land in total 29.875 decimals from Jahir Ali and his two brothers by 6 kabalas dated 1-2-1990, 16-11-1974, 12-12-1974 and 12-4-1975 and by 2 more kabalas, both dated 22-4-1975. They have been possessing the purchased lands by constructing building thereon.

9. The defendants Nos. 2(ka)-2(kha), 4-12 and 13 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 filed written statement separately. Their case are that Jahir Ali and his brother Junayed Ali together sold 0.1225 acres to the defendant No.13 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 on different dates. The defendant Nos. 4-12 purchased 0.1175 acres on different date from Jahir Ali and his brothers. The defendant No.2 purchased 0.0550 acres from Jahir Ali and his brother.

10. The case of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 in brief, is that the predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants Charan Ram Malakar were owners of the first schedule land as described in schedule to the plaint. Subsequently, the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants became successive owners by inheritance, Gagan Ram and his 2 brothers, predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendant Nos. 9-10 during their life time produced CS Khatian and other documents before the employee of settlement Jarip at the time of preparation of SA Khatian. They believed SA Khatian was prepared in their names. The predecessors of the plaintiffs for their convenience of enjoyment partitioned the suit land along with other lands and accordingly Gagan Ram Malakar got the suit land in his saham. The plaintiffs filled up the suit land with earth. But the defendant Nos. 3-8 evicted the plaintiffs from the suit second schedule land by constructing tin shed building. The plaintiff on several times requested the defendant Nos.3-8 to leave the suit second schedule land in their favour. But the defendants claimed that the land of second schedule was recorded in the name of Government and they took lease from the Government. On searching in the local Tahsil Office, the plaintiffs came to know on 18-2-2014 that the land of first schedule of plaint was recorded in SA Khatian as canal খাল which was incorrect. In fact the suit land should be recorded as সাইলউরা in CS Khatian in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs and the pro-forma defendants. Thus the plaintiffs were cons-trained to file the suit for declaration of title by adverse possession for statutory period of 12 years in respect of first schedule land, decla-ration that SA Khatian is wrong in respect of first schedule land and Khas possession in respect of second schedule land as described in schedule to plaint.

11. The defendant No.3 and the defendant Nos.11-22 contested the suit by filing separate written statement. The statements of the defendant No. 3 is same to the statements of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 which was discussed above. The case of the defendants Nos.11-22 is that the First schedule land is a part of Fulbari Mouja. The First Schedule land had no existence in Tikorbari Mouja. Jahir Ali, the predecessor of these defendants purchased the schedule land along with other lands from the Original owner Gokul Malakar and others on 24-4-1952. Jahir All and his two brothers Jayed Ali and Tasir Ali, while possessing the suit land, Tasir Ali died. Thereafter Jahir Ali and Jonayed All sold 0.06 acres to Serajuddin, Jahir All and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 4 Jaista 3 pon,10 Gonda to the defendants No.11 on 1-2-1970 by saf kabala. Then Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0625 acres to the predecessor of defendant Nos. 13-21 on 7-11-1974. Again on 16-11-1974 Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0150 acres to the mother of defendant No.11 and grandmother of defendant Nos.13-21. Subsequently, Jahir Ali and the heirs of Tasir Ali sold 0.0625 acres, 0.0550 acres 0.0550 acres, to defendant No.12, Abdur Rahman, the predecessor of defendant Nos.13-22 and the defendant No.11 respectively and after selling the aforesaid lands Jahir All and his brothers had no land in suit jote.

12. On Scrutiny the pleadings of the above mentioned suits i.e. Title Suit Nos.32 of 1997/51 of 2001, 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 and 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 the trial court had framed the issues as follows:

১. আনীত আকারে ও প্রকারে মোকদ্দমাত্রয় চলিতে পারে কিনা?

২. মোকদ্বমাত্রয়ে পক্ষদোধ আছে কিনা?

৩. মোকদ্দমাত্রয়ে তামাদি দোষ আছে কিনা?

৪. স্বতু ৯৩/৯৪ ইং মোকদ্দমার নালিশি ১ম তপসীলের ভূমিতে এ মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষের স্বত্ব আছে কিনা এবং এ মোকদমার ২য় তপসীলের ভূমিতে এ মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষের স্বত্ দখল আছে কিনা?

৫. স্বত্ব ৫১/০১ ইং মোকদ্দমার নালিশি ভূমি সংক্রান্ত তর্কিত ২৪-৪-১৯৫২ ইং তারিখে ৭১৯ নং কবলাটি খাই খালাসী বন্ধকী কবলা কিনা এবং উক্ত কবলাভুক্ত ভূমি বাবদ উক্ত মামলার বাদীগণ খাস দখল পাওয়ার হকদার কিনা?

৬. স্বত্ব ৫২/০১ ইং মোকদ্মার প্রথম তপসীলের ভূমিতে এ মোকদ্দমার বাদীগণের স্বত্ দখল আছে কিনা এবং উক্ত ভূমি বাবদ সেটেলমেন্ট জরিপী রেকর্ড ভ্রমাতুক মর্মে ঘোষণা করার কারণ আছে কিনা?

৭. স্বত্ব ৫২/০১ ইং মোকদ্দমায় ২য় তপসীলের ভূমিতে এ মোকদ্দমার বাদীগণের দখল ছিল কিনা এবং বর্ণিত মতে

বাদীগণ ৩-৮ নং বিবাদীগণ কর্তৃক এ ভূমি হইতে বেদখল হইয়াছিল কিনা?

৮. স্বত্ব ৯৩/৯৪ ইং মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থিত মতে আরজির ১ম তপসীলের ভূমি বাবদ বন্টনের প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি এবং আরজির ২য় তপসীলের ভূমি বাবদ স্বত্ব ঘোষণার ডিক্রি পাইতে পারে কিনা?

৯. স্বতু ৫১/০১ ইং মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষ প্রার্থিত মতে নালিশি ভূমি বাবদ খাই খালাসী বন্ধক মুক্তত্রমে খাস দখলের ডিক্রি পাইতে পারে কিনা?

১০. স্বত্ব ৫২/০১ ইং মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষ আরজির ১ম তপসীলের ভূমি বাবদ প্রার্থিত উভয় ঘোষণামূলক এবং

আরজির ২য তপসীলের ভূমি বাবদ খাস দখলের ডিক্রি পাইতে পারে কিনা?

13. Manik Mia, the plaintiff No.1 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 deposed on behalf of all plaintiffs as PW 1 on Commission and 3 more witnesses were examined as PWs 2-4 and the documents produced by them were marked as Exhibit ক-ছ and Exhibits-x-x(1).

14. Gakul Ram Malakar, the plaintiff No. 1 of Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 and Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 deposed on behalf of all the plaintiffs as PW 1 on Commission and three more witnesses were examined as 2-4.

15. Defendant Nos. 5-16 adduced 5 DWs to prove their case and documents produced by them were marked as Exhibit: ক১-ট১১.

16. On considering the oral and documentary evidences the trial court decreed the Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 against the contesting defendant Nos.1 and 5-16 and ex-parte against the rest, dismissed the Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 against the contesting defendant Nos. 16-18 and 2ka, 2(kha) and defendant Nos. 4-13 and ex-parte against the rest and also dismissed the Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 against the contesting defendant Nos. 3 and 11-22 and ex-parte against the rest.

17. Being aggrieved by judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008, the defendant Nos. 5-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 as appellants preferred First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 and the heirs of defendant No.13 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 preferred First Appeal No. 230 of 2009. It is pertinent to note that the appellants of the said First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 claimed ownership through purchase some portion of the land from the chronological recipient of the kabala in question dated 24-4-1952. The appellants claimed the said deed is out and out sale. But the learned trial court decreed the Title Suit. No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 considering the said deed in question is mortgage deed and, as such, they filed the instant First Appeal No. 230 of 2009.

18. In the same way being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008, the plaintiffs 1-7 of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 147 of 2009 before the District Judge, Sylhet which was subsequently transferred to the High Court Division and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No. 1 of 2014.

19. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the same judgment and decree the plaintiff Nos.1-3 of Title Suit No. 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 108 of 2009 before District Judge, Sylhet which was being transferred to the High Court Division and re-numbered as Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014.

20. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate on behalf of defendants Nos.5-16 appellants of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 submits that the root of disputes between the parties based on the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS and the agreement for reconveyance of the said land executed on the same date stipulated a period of 3 years from the said date that is to say, the time for reconveyance expired on 30th chaitra 1361 corresponding to 24-4-1956 and the said transaction is not attracted by section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He further submits that a transaction by way of out and out sale with an separate agreement to reconvay deed was not a mortgage before coming into effect of the Presidents Order (PO 88 of 1972) read with Presidents Order 136 of 1972, because of facts such transaction was not a mortgage by definition of "Mortgage" as provided in section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act. He next submits that where the agreement to recovery is embodied in the same document by which sale is effected the transaction is conditional mortgage. He also submits that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to recovery which has been treated to be mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and same was not alive on 3-8-1972, the date of coming into effect of the Presidents Order 88 of 1972. He further submits such transaction is past and closed and the property involved in such transaction will not be redeemable. He finally submits that the trial court erroneously held that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage for 7 years and ignoring the doctrine past and closed decreed the Title Suit No.51 of 2001 for redemption of mortgage and khas of possession in respect of 0.34 acres of suit land is totally illegal. In support of his submissions learned advocate referred the decision reported in 32 DLR(AD) 233, 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90 and 1 BLC (AD) 164.

21. Mr Anwarul Azim Khair, the learned Advocate on behalf of the appellants of First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 adopted the arguments Advanced by the learned Advocate for the 5-16 defendants Nos. 5-16 appellants of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009. In addition he submits that the transaction in question of the present case is not itself mortgaged within the mischief of section 58 of Transfer Property Act. Section 58 of Transfer Property Act states about different kind of mortgage. He next submits sale deed and condition embodied in the same deed is called mortgage deed. But when the sale deed with an separate reconveyance deed, it shall come within the mischief of section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Finally he submits section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, was challenged in High Court Division by filing writ which was allowed and against which Leave to Appeal has been filed. In 32 DLR (AD) in para-11 it was discussed elaborately and was upheld.

22. Mr Sadananda Rana, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondents-defendants 1 and 2 of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 submits that the trial court rightly found the deed in question being NO.719 dated 24-4-1952 is a mortgage deed. Section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, has been amended by the Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 with effect from 3 August 1972, but this amendment did not touch the period of a usufructuary mortgage which  is still 7 years, nor did it effect the period of limitation for redemption suit which is 60 years. section 95A was incorporated after amendment of section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, by President Order 86 of 1972 which gives the mortgagor, the right to get his property by application to a Magistrate. This amendment gives an out and Out sale with a condition of reconveyance will still be treated. a complete usufructuary mortgage. Tits amendment says on the expiry of the period of a mortgage, the mortgagee does not restore possession of the land to the mortgagor, on the application of the mortgagor, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate will restore the possession to the mortgagor. On the other hand, for getting back possession of a mortgaged land the mortgagor need not file any redemption suit, but may get remedy by an application to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. He next submits after insertion new section of 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, any transfer of a land by an out and out sale with a condition for reconveyance shall be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding 7 years on the expiry of which the mortgagor may get back possession by an application to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. He finally submits that once a mortgage is always mortgage, and, as such, the doctrine of past and closed transaction is not applicable. In support of his submission, he referred the decision reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237, 3 BLT 135, 12 MLR (AD) 26, 52 DLR (AD) 152 and 36 DLR 90.

23. Mr Dider Alam Kollol, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of Transfer Appeal No. 2 of 2014 argued that the learned trial court without considering the evidence of the plaintiff appellants reached into erroneous decision. CS Khatian was filed by the original owner Charan Ram Malakar which was marked as Exhibit-1. But the learned court erroneously found that the plaintiff could not file documents in his support. In the plaint it was specifically mentioned that the plaintiffs were evicted by the defendants on first part of poush in 1400 BS. But the court below did not consider it. He finally submits the trial court in its judgment did not mention about the commissioners report which is totally misconceived on law. He also argued that learned court below on misconception of law found the deed in question dated 24-4-1952 is a mortgage deed. In fact that deed is within the mischief of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but it was not alive at the date of commencement of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 on 3-8-1972. So, the said transaction does not attract section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Jahir Ali became owner on the basis of deed No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 and subsequently after selling the property 0.7 decimals remain with Jahir Ali. After death of Jahir Ali his heirs the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and plaintiff of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 became owner and they are entitled for partition of 0.7 decimals of land.

24. In reply the learned Advocate Mr Khan Ezaz Maswood argued that the heirs of Jahir Ali will not get 0.7 decimals of land for partition as the heirs of Jahir Ali did not pray for declaration of title over 0.7 decimals of land. Moreover Md Manik Miah son of Jahir Ali deposed as PW 1 in Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 that 0.33 decimals of land was sold out by Jahir Ali and 02 decimals of land was acquired by CNB. The total disputed land is 0.34 decimals. So, the heirs of Jahir Ali will not get partition for 0.7 decimals as prayed for and the learned court did not commit any error of law and facts by dismissing the Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994.

25. Heard the learned Advocate of the respective parties examined the evidences oral and documentary and materials on record.

26. Admittedly the first schedule land of three Suits i.e. Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 and Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 were originally belonged by Charan Ram Malakar. It may be noted that total land of first schedule to the plaint of three suits are 1 kader, 1 powa, 4 jaista in local measurement equivalent to 39 acres as argued by learned Advocate Khair Ezaz Maswood. Charan Ram Malakar died leaving behind 4 sons namely, Gagan Ram Malakar, Behari Ram Malakar, Raman Ram Malakar and Avoy Ram Malakar. Behari Ram Malakar died leaving behind 3 brothers as childless. Raman Ram Malakar died leaving behind two sons namely Naresh Ram Malakar, Gopesh Ram Malakar (pro-forma defendant Nos.3 and 4 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001). Then Avoy Ram Malakar died leaving only brother Gagan Ram Malakar. During the life time of Gagan Ram Malakar, Raman Ram Malakar, Avoy Ram Malakar they executed a registered sale deed on 24-4-1952 corres-ponding to 11-1-1359 BS in favour of Jahir Ali (father of Abdul Manik and Mst Sabiya Begum of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001) receiving Rupees 100 only and on the same date Jahir Ali executed a registered Ekrarnama Deed in favour of Gagan Ram Malakar, Roman Ram Malakar and Avoy Ram Malakar. It was stipulated in the Ekrarnama deed that the consideration money Rupees 100 will be paid back by 30th chaittra 1361 BS i.e. within 3 years.

27. It is alleged by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and Title Suit No: 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 and defendant Nos.16-20 of Title Suit No. 14 of 1994/93 of 1994 that the deed in question dated 24. 04.1952 was never a sale deed. It was a usufractuary Mortgage within the mischief of section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It is also alleged that the consideration money was paid and moreover it should be re-deemed after 7 years as per section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

28. It is alleged by the defendant Nos. 5-16 of Title Suit No. 32 of 1997/51 of 2001 the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 the defendant Nos.3, 11-22 of Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 that the deed in question dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS and on the same date the agreement for reconveyance was executed which is not mortgage as defined in section 58 of the Transfer Property Act. In other words, it was not a mortgage proper before 3-8-1972 (the date of coming into effect of President Order No. 88 of 1972 and President Order No. 136 of 1972). By the said president Order the deed in question dated 24-4-1952 was treated to be mortgage. But the deed in question was not alive on 3-8-1972 inasmuch as the period mentioned in the Deed of reconveyance was fixed to reconvey the land by 30 chaittra, 1361 BS i.e within 3 years of the Deed which had expired long before 3-8-1972. So, the transaction of the deed in question is past and closed and it was not liable to be redeemed. This deed in question is treated to be mortgage. The defendant appellants are owners by subsequent purchase and they have been possessing the suit land.

29. The core issue in this appeal is that whether the Deed No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 and reconveyance deed No.720 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X, X(I) are the basic documents upon which the parties claimed their respective title is complete usufructary mortgage or treated to be mortgage under section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and whether the deed in question is attracted to section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

30. To determine this question, we like to quote he deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X) and also the Deed of agreement being No. 720 (Exhibit No.X(i) executed on the same date.

32. The Deed of Agreement being No. 720 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X(i) describes as follows:

“........... ইয়াদি কির্দ্দ ১) রমন রাম মালাকার, ২) গগন রাম মালাকার, ৩) অভয় রাম মালাকার, সাং-ফুল বাড়ী, পং-বরায়া, জাতি-হিন্দু, পিতা-মৃত-চরন রাম মালাকার, ব্যবসা-গৃহসি, জিলা-সিলেট, থানা-গোলাপগঞ্জ বরাবরেষু লিখিতং জহির আলী, পিতা-মৃত সাং-কাজন, সাং-টাকর বাড়ী পং বরায়া, জাতি-মোসলমান ব্যবসা গৃহস্থি, জিলা-সিলেট, থানা-গোলাপগঞ্জ ৷ অদ্য একরারনামা পত্র মিদং, জিলা-সিলেট, থানা-গোলাপঞ্জ। সিলেট সদর সাব রেজিষ্ট্রার সাহেবের এলাকাধীন আমি অদ্য তারিখে তোমাদের নিকট হইতে নিম্নের তপসীলের লিখিত পরগণা ও মৌজা ও মহাল ও কিত্তা সংক্রান্ত মোঃ/১।৪ এক কেদার এক পোয়া চারি জষ্টি জমি বাৎসরিক মং ৪, চারি টাকা খাজনায় মং ১০০ এক শত টাকায় খরিদ করিয়াছি সেমতে আমি অত্র একরারনামা পত্র লিখিয়া দিয়া একরার করিতেছি। সে অদ্য হইতে আগামী সন ১৩৬১ বাংলার ৩০শা চৈত্র তারিখের মধ্যে মদি উপরের লিখিত অজয় মালের মং ১০০, একশত টাকা তোমরা কি তোমরার অভাবে তোমাদের উত্তরাধি কি আমার অভাবে আমার উত্তরাধিকে ফেরত দেন তবে আমি কি আমার উত্তরাধিকারী উক্ত জমা জমি তোমার কি তোমাদের উত্তরাধিকে অজয় মালীর উক্ত মং ১০০, এক শত টাকা গ্রহণ পূর্বক কবলা সম্পাদন করিয়া জমা জমি আপন দখল হইতে ছাড়িয়া দিব। ও তোমাদের দস্তখত অদ্য তারিখের লিখিত কবলা সাক্ষরও সাক্ষী আবদুর রহিম সাং দাড়িপাতন পং বরায়া (২য় ফর্দ) খানা ও তোমাদিগকে ওয়াপেশ দিব, আর যদি উপরের লিখিত ম্যায়াদ মধ্যে অজয় মালীর টাকা ফেরত দিতে না পারেন তবে উক্ত জমাজমি ফেরত দিবায় । কোন প্রকার দাবী কোন আদালতে কি কোন পঞ্চায়তে চলিবে না, এতদর্থে সদজ্ঞানে সুস্থ শরীরে থাকিয়া অত্র একরারনামা পত্র লিখিয়া দিলাম। ইতি ২৪-৪-১৯৫২ মোঃ ১২-১-১৯৫৯ বাংলা তপসীল চতুঃ সীমানা পং বরায়া মৌজা ফুলবাড়ীস্থিত ৬২৮৮/১০ নং তাং মাং হুসন সংক্রান্ত মং ৪, চারি টাকার খাজনা মুক্ত জুত জমির সীমানা ১। কিন্তে জমির তল কেঃ জঃ। ৪৫৭৮ দাগ পুঃ সড়ক পং জুত এজমালী উং বিক্রি ২ দাগের জমি দং জুত বৈকুন্ট রামমালী এহাতে মোং০।। ২ দুঃ কমলা রকম ভূমি ২। কিত্তে এ কেং জঃ ৪৫৭৯ দাগ পুঃ সড়ক পং জুত করম আলী উং সড়ক দং বিক্রিত ১ দাগের জমি ও জুত ব্রজ মালী এহাতে মোং দ২ দুঃ ফসল রকম ভূমি মোট মোঃ......”

33. It appears from the recital of those documents that:

i) Sale deed, ii) separate registered re-conveyance deed, the period of repayment for 3 years i. e. 30th Chaittra 1361 BS, iii) Possession was delivered.

34. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates, now we can look into the definition of "Treated to be mortgage" under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.

95A Treatment of certain transaction as usufructuary mortgage—

Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, 2[either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey,] 3[or] where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Second Amendment) Order, 1972] (President's Order No. 88 of 1972).

35. On careful reading the registered saf kabala deed dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS (Exhibit-X) and the deed of reconveyance on the same date (Exhibit-X-(1), it appears that the predecessors of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 sold the suit property i.e. 1 Kader, 1 powa 4 jaista in local measurement to Jahir Ali, father of defendant Nos.1 and 2 of said suit with a condition of re-purchase of the same within 3 years that is 30th chaittra 1361 corresponding to 24-4-1956.

36. The learned Advocate Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, argued that an out and out sale accompanied by an agreement for reconveyance is within the purview of the Presidents Order Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 and No.24 of 1973 whereby provisions of section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been amended and a new section being section 95A has been inserted in the said Act. The Presidents Order No.88 of 1972 came into effect on 3-8-1972 (PO No.136 of 1972) and the condition giving right of repurchase having expired the sale became a past and closed transaction and on the same reason the plaintiffs are not entitled for redemption of mortgage of the suit land. In this respect he referred the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD), 233.

37. We have gone through the decision reported in 32 DLR, 233. It appears that in that Writ Petition No. 85 of 1974 along with good number of Writ Petitions were heard analogously. The facts of the said Writ Petition was that the respondent No.1 purchased the land from the respondent No.3 with an agreement to reconvey the said land. The agreement was dated 26-4-1963 which stipulated that the land will be reconveyed if the money is repaid within 10 years. The respondent No.3 i.e. mortgagor made an application before Sub-Divisional Magistrate for restoration of the mortgaged property under section 9(4) and 9(5) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and same was allowed on 30-3-1973. Then the said writ petitions were filed challenging the section 95A of the aforesaid Act which were made absolute and against the said judgment appeals were filed. It has been held by Appellate Division in their judgment that: "Our conclusions, therefore, are that the President's Order Nos.88 and 136 of 1972 and No.24 of 1973 are all valid legislation for affecting necessary amendments in the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and those laws cannot be attacked on the ground of ultravires. (2) any transfer of a holding or part thereof by a raiyat either way of out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and transferee acquires the right to possess and enjoy the usufruct, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of maximum 7 years and the provisions of section 95(4) and (5) shall apply to such transfers; (3) and such transfers are not to be understood in the light of the Transfer of Property Act because those are to be understood in the light of the enactment in question: (4) those transactions which are subsisting on the date of promulgation of President's Order No.88 of 1972 are hit by section 95A including the transaction entered into by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to recovery, made whether before or after the promulgation of President's Order No.88 of 1972: and (5) as for the transactions which are not alive before the promulgation of President's Order No.88 of 1972 they are concluded by the transactions past and closed."

38. Though the facts and circumstances of the cited case and the present case are different,

but the decision made to the effect that the transaction which were not alive, at the promulgation of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 on 3-8-1972 is within the mischief of doctrine past and closed, that is similar to present transaction that the deed in question being No.719 dated 24-4-1952 was not alive on 3-8-1972 at the promulgation of President Order No.88 of 1972.

39. On the contrary, the learned Advocate Sadananda Rana having referred the decisions reported in 34 DLR (AD) 258, 12 MLR (AD) 329, 52 DLR (AD) 152, and 36 DLR 90 submits the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 with an registered agreement No. 720 dated 24-4-1952 is an out and out sale with a condition to reconvey is a complete usufructuary mortgage.

<u>40. On scrutinize those decisions, the sale deed of the cited cases reported in 34 DLR (AD) 238, 52 DLR (AD) 133 and 12 MLR (AD) 329 is by one single document wherein the condition embodied to reconvey on certain date. But the pr6sent transaction is not made by a single document but the deed in question is out and out sale with an separate registered agreement deed to reconvey within 3 (three) years which expired long before the promulgation of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 on 3-8-972. The sale deed of the cited case reported in 36 DLR 90 was registered on 20-5-1970 as well as a registered agreement was executed with condition to reconvey within 10 years which means the transaction was alive on 3-8-1972 at the promulgation of President Order No. 88 of 1972. So, those citations referred by the learned Advocate for respondents of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 have no nexus with the facts and circumstances of the present case.</u>

<u>41. Therefore Exhibit-X, X(i) coupled with section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233, 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90, 1 BLC (AD) 164 clearly proved that the deed in question being No.719 dated 24-4-1952 with registered agreement deed being No.720 dated 24-4-1952 treated to be mortgage but since the transaction was not alive on 3-8-1972, at the promulgation of President Order 88 of 1972, the said transaction is not hit by section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.</u>

42. Therefore, we find the trial court held the deed in question being No.719 dated 24-4-1952 with an agreement to reconvey being 720 dated 24- 4-1952 constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage for a maximum period of 7 years based on totally misconception of law and facts. So, the decree passed by the trial court for re-deemption of mortgage and khas possession in favour of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 is erroneous.

43. Similarly in Title Suit No.15 of 1994/52 of 2001 the plaintiffs claimed title on the basis of the sale Deed No.719 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X) and reconveyance Deed No. 720 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X-(1) is not proved mortgage at all under section 58 of Transfer of Property Act and the learned trial court rightly dismissed the said suit. Though the trial court dismissed the suit on different findings that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title and possession over the suit land and also failed to prove the dispossession from the suit land. So, we can easily rely on the decision reported in 32 DLR (AD), 233 which has been subsequently followed in the decision reported in 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90, 1 BLC (AD) 164.

44. In Title Suit No.14 of 1994/93 of 1994 the heirs of Jahir Ali, Md Manik Mia and Sabiya Begum sought for partition in respect of 0.7 decimals of land as described in First Schedule of land and declaration for 0.02 decimals as described in second Schedule land to the plaint. Manik Mia as PW 1 in Title Suit No. 93 of 1994 in his chief stated:

“………… এই নালিশী ভূমি আমার পিতার খরিদা ভূমি এক কেদার ১ পোয়া ৪ জষ্টি। ইহার মধ্যে ৩৩ শতক বিক্রিত। অবশিষ্ট ভূমি আমি এবং আমার চাচাত ভাইরা যৌথভাবে ভোগ দখলে আছি……. ২ শতক জায়গা সি এন্ড বি এর নামে রেকর্ড হইয়া গেলেও আমরা ভোগ দখলে আছি।”

44. It is important to note that the second schedule land is from Tikorbari Mouja. But the lands of the deed in question being No.719 dated 24-4-1952 situated in Fulbari Mouja. But the present dispute between the parties in respect of land of Fulbari Mouja. So, the land of second schedule has no nexus with the land of Fulbari Mouja which arises the dispute between the parties. On the other hand, the land of second schedule property is unspecified as there is no boundary. Therefore, declaration for unspecified land is not maintainable and further no averment was made in the plaint to show the date of dispossession.

46. The plaintiff No.1, Manik Mia, (son of Jahir Ali) admitted in his deposition that they had no title over 0.2 decimals out of 0.7 decimals. So, in this respect without praying for declaration of title, the suit for partition over 0.7 decimals is not maintainable. Moreover, Md Manik Mia, son of jahir Ali categorically stated in his chief that they sold 0.33 decimals. Thus it is evident that the second schedule land is from different Mouja which is not disputed in the suit and without declaration of title, the relief sought only for partition in respect of 0.7 decimals is not maintainable and the trial court rightly dismissed the suit.

47. The defendant Nos. 5-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 claimed they purchased 29.875 decimals by Exhibit-খ২,গ৩,ঘ৪,ঙ৫,চ৬, from Jahir Ali. On perusal of those Exhibits it appears by Exhibit- খ২,গ৩,ঘ৪,ঙ৫,চ৬, an area of land is 0.0425, 0.0625, 0.0625, 0.0550, 0.0550 respectively in total 28.75 decimals of land were purchased. Gokul Ram Malakar the plaintiff  No.1 of Title Suit Nos.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 and 15 of 1994/52 of 2001 admitted in cross stating that Jahir Ali sold his maximum property to Abdur Rahman and others. It may be mentioned that defendant Nos.7-16 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 are heirs of Abdur

Rahman, the defendant Nos.5-6 are Abdus Sattar and his wife. Manik Mia as PW 1 of Title Suit No.32 of 1997/5 of 2001 in cross admitted that his father sold those lands. Thus it is proved that defendant Nos.5-16 became owners of total 28.75 decimals of land through purchase by Exhibits, খ২,গ৩,ঘ৪,ঙ৫,চ৬, respectively from Jahir Ali, father of plaintiff.

48. Having regard to facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the deed being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 upon which parties are claiming their respective title, the trial court on misconception of law and facts most illegally held the said deed is out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey constituted to be usufructuary mortgage for 7 years and on that basis decreed the Title Suit No. 51 of 2001 for redemption of mortgage and khas possession. Since we have found that heirs of Jahir Ali failed to prove the suit for partition over 0.7 decimals, and 0.2 decimals for declaration of title which is situated in different mouja and unspecified that has no nexus with the present claim, so the trial court rightly dismissed the Title Suit No. 93 of 1994 and Title Suit No. 52 of 2001.

49. In the result the First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 is allowed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet decreeing the Title Suit No.32 of 1997/51 of 2001 is set aside and the suit is dismissed.

50. First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 is allowed with modification that the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 is treated to be a mortgage but since the said deed is not alive on 3-8-1972 at the time of promulgation of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 is not hit under section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.

51. Transfer Appeal No.1 of 2014 and Transfer Appeal No.2 of 2014 are hereby dismissed without order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-2008 are confirmed.

Send down the lower court records along with a copy of this judgment at once.
